name: Sports trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about rules, famous athletes, events and records that no longer change. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: The standard marathon distance of 42.195 km traces back to the Olympic Games held in which city?
items.explain: The 1908 London Olympic marathon was run over 26 miles 385 yards (42.195 km). That distance became the official standard in 1921.

source.title: Athletics at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon

items.question: In which year did women first compete in an Olympic marathon?
items.explain: The women's Olympic marathon made its debut at the 1984 Games in Los Angeles.

items.question: Which Ethiopian runner won the Olympic marathon in both 1960 and 1964?
items.explain: Abebe Bikila won the Olympic marathon in 1960 and again in 1964, the first man to win it twice.

items.question: Which friend of Pierre de Coubertin suggested adding a marathon to the first modern Olympics?
items.explain: Michel Bréal proposed the race to Coubertin, basing it on the legend of a messenger running from the Battle of Marathon to Athens.

items.question: On which Oxford track did Roger Bannister run the first sub-four-minute mile in 1954?
items.explain: Bannister ran his record mile at Oxford University's Iffley Road track on 6 May 1954. The track has since been renamed in his honour.

items.question: What was Roger Bannister's time when he first broke four minutes for the mile in 1954?
items.explain: Bannister was timed at 3 minutes 59.4 seconds on 6 May 1954. Landy's 3:57.9 came a few weeks later.

source.title: A Brief History of the Sub-4-Minute Mile

items.question: Which Australian miler broke four minutes weeks after Bannister and later lost to him in the 1954 "Miracle Mile" at Vancouver?
items.explain: John Landy ran 3:58 in Finland in June 1954. Bannister then beat him at the Empire Games in Vancouver, where both men went under four minutes.

source.title: A Brief History of the Sub-4-Minute Mile

items.question: Which runner set the pace for the first two laps of Bannister's record mile?
items.explain: Chris Brasher led the first two laps, reaching halfway in 1:58. Chris Chataway then took over before Bannister sprinted past him.

items.question: Which American matched Jesse Owens's four track-and-field gold medals at a single Olympics in 1984?
items.explain: Owens's four-gold haul at Berlin 1936 stood alone until Carl Lewis matched it at Los Angeles in 1984.

source.title: How Jesse Owens Foiled Hitler's Plans for the 1936 Olympics

items.question: Jesse Owens's 200 m silver medallist in 1936, Mack Robinson, was the older brother of which future baseball star?
items.explain: Mack Robinson finished second to Owens in the 200 m. His younger brother Jackie later broke baseball's colour barrier.

source.title: Virtual Exhibit: Jesse Owens' incredible performance at Berlin 1936

items.question: Which German long jumper advised Jesse Owens during qualifying in 1936 and went on to win silver behind him?
items.explain: Luz Long's advice helped Owens qualify for the long jump final. Owens took gold and Long took silver.

source.title: Jesse Owens' achievements at 1936 Olympics were 'thumb in the eye' to Adolf Hitler, says US athlete's grandson

items.question: What score did the scoreboard show after Nadia Comăneci's first perfect routine at Montreal 1976?
items.explain: The scoreboard could not display a 10.00, so her perfect 10 appeared as 1.00.

items.question: On which apparatus did Nadia Comăneci score her first perfect 10 in 1976?
items.explain: Her first 10.0 came on the uneven parallel bars on 18 July 1976.

items.question: How many perfect 10.0 scores did Nadia Comăneci receive at the 1976 Montreal Olympics?
items.explain: She received seven perfect scores in Montreal and won three gold medals.

items.question: Which official timing company asked how many digits the Montreal 1976 gymnastics scoreboard needed, and was told three would do?
items.explain: Omega, the Olympic timers, were told a 10.00 would not be possible, so the board showed only three digits.

items.question: By roughly how much did Bob Beamon beat the previous long jump world record at the 1968 Olympics?
items.explain: His 8.90 m jump bettered the existing world record by 55 cm. No earlier single jump had improved it by more than 15 cm.

items.question: Which American broke Bob Beamon's long jump world record at the 1991 World Championships in Tokyo?
items.explain: Mike Powell jumped 8.95 m in Tokyo in 1991, ending Beamon's world record.

items.question: For how many years did Bob Beamon's 1968 long jump stand as the world record?
items.explain: It lasted 23 years, from 1968 until Mike Powell's jump in 1991.

items.question: Which team did Wilt Chamberlain score 100 points against on 2 March 1962?
items.explain: Chamberlain scored 100 for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169–147 win over the New York Knicks.

items.question: In which Pennsylvania town was Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game played?
items.explain: The game was played at the Hershey Sports Arena in front of about 4,000 fans.

items.question: What was Wilt Chamberlain's scoring average for the 1961–62 season, the year of his 100-point game?
items.explain: Chamberlain averaged 50.4 points per game that season, up from 38.4 the year before.

items.question: Before his 100-point night, what was the overall NBA single-game scoring record, set by Chamberlain himself earlier in 1961–62?
items.explain: Chamberlain's 78-point game earlier that season was the previous overall record, which his 100 then replaced.

items.question: How many runs did Don Bradman need in his final Test innings to finish with a career batting average of exactly 100?
items.explain: Bradman needed just four runs but was dismissed for a duck. That left him on 99.94.

items.question: Which England leg-spinner bowled Don Bradman for a duck in his final Test innings in 1948?
items.explain: Eric Hollies bowled Bradman with a googly for 0, leaving his career average at 99.94.

items.question: At which ground did Don Bradman play his famous final Test innings in 1948?
items.explain: His duck came at The Oval in London in the 1948 Ashes series.

items.question: For how many consecutive games did Joe DiMaggio hit safely in 1941?
items.explain: DiMaggio hit in 56 straight games from 15 May to 16 July 1941, still the longest streak in Major League history.

source.title: Longest hitting streaks in MLB history

items.question: Against which team was Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak snapped on 17 July 1941?
items.explain: DiMaggio went hitless in Cleveland, where third baseman Ken Keltner twice robbed him of hits.

items.question: Which Cincinnati Reds player hit safely in 44 straight games in 1978?
items.explain: Pete Rose's 44-game streak in 1978 is the third-longest in MLB history.

source.title: Longest hitting streaks in MLB history

items.question: Which Yankees catcher leapt into Don Larsen's arms after his perfect game in the 1956 World Series?
items.explain: Yogi Berra caught Larsen's perfect game and famously jumped into his arms after the final out.

source.title: New York Yankees' Don Larsen pitches only World Series perfect game

items.question: Which team did Don Larsen's Yankees face when he pitched his World Series perfect game in 1956?
items.explain: Larsen retired all 27 Brooklyn Dodgers he faced in Game 5 at Yankee Stadium.

items.question: Whom did Don Larsen strike out for the final out of his 1956 World Series perfect game?
items.explain: Larsen struck out Dale Mitchell on a 1–2 pitch to complete the perfect game.

source.title: New York Yankees' Don Larsen pitches only World Series perfect game

items.question: In which city did Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman in the 1974 "Rumble in the Jungle"?
items.explain: The fight took place in Kinshasa, then in Zaire and now in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

items.question: Which strategy did Muhammad Ali use against George Foreman by leaning on the ropes and letting him tire himself out?
items.explain: Ali's rope-a-dope had him lean against the ropes and absorb punches while Foreman wore himself out.

items.question: In which round did Muhammad Ali knock out George Foreman in the Rumble in the Jungle?
items.explain: Ali knocked Foreman out in the eighth round to regain the heavyweight title.

items.question: Which promoter, then new to boxing, arranged the Ali–Foreman fight in Zaire?
items.explain: Don King, an ex-convict new to promoting, arranged the bout and secured record $5 million purses for both fighters.

source.title: Rumble in the Jungle | EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: What was the final score of the "Miracle on Ice" game between the United States and the Soviet Union in 1980?
items.explain: The underdog US team beat the four-time defending champion Soviets 4–3 at Lake Placid on 22 February 1980.

items.question: Who coached the US men's ice hockey team that won gold at the 1980 Winter Olympics?
items.explain: Herb Brooks coached the team of college players that beat the Soviets and went on to win gold.

source.title: When the US Olympic Hockey Team Stunned the World

items.question: Which team did the US beat in 1980 to secure the gold medal, two days after the Miracle on Ice?
items.explain: The US needed to beat Finland after the Soviet game. They came from behind to win 4–2 and take gold.

items.question: Which sports announcer's famous call gave the "Miracle on Ice" its name?
items.explain: The name "Miracle on Ice" comes from a famous call by Al Michaels.

items.question: Which England goalkeeper was beaten by Maradona's "Hand of God" goal at the 1986 World Cup?
items.explain: Maradona outjumped Peter Shilton and punched the ball into the net in the quarter-final. Argentina won 2–1.

source.title: Famous FIFA World Cup Goals: 'Hand of God' | Britannica

items.question: Which team did Argentina beat in the 1986 World Cup final, after Maradona's goals against England?
items.explain: Argentina beat West Germany 3–2 in the final to win the 1986 World Cup.

source.title: 30 years on: Maradona's 'hand of God' | UEFA.com

items.question: Who won the first Olympic marathon at the 1896 Athens Games?
items.explain: Greek runner Spyridon Louis won the first Olympic marathon in 1896, to great national celebration.

items.question: Who was elected the first president of the International Olympic Committee after the 1894 congress?
items.explain: The Greek Demetrius Vikelas was elected the IOC's first president. Coubertin succeeded him after the 1896 Games.

items.question: Which Roman emperor banned the ancient Olympic Games, roughly 1,500 years before they were revived in 1896?
items.explain: Emperor Theodosius I banned the ancient Games, and they were reborn in Athens in 1896.

items.question: In which two years did Rod Laver win all four major tennis singles titles in one calendar year?
items.explain: Laver completed the calendar-year Grand Slam in 1962 as an amateur and again in 1969.

items.question: Rod Laver was the second man to win a calendar-year Grand Slam. Who was the first, in 1938?
items.explain: Don Budge won all four majors in 1938, before Laver became the second man to do so in 1962.

items.question: Whom did Rod Laver beat in the 1969 US Open final to complete his second calendar-year Grand Slam?
items.explain: Laver beat fellow Australian Tony Roche in four sets in the final on 9 September 1969.

source.title: The day Laver won the calendar Grand Slam AGAIN!! - Tennis Majors

items.question: Whom did Steffi Graf beat in the 1988 Olympic final in Seoul to complete her "Golden Slam"?
items.explain: Graf beat Argentina's Gabriela Sabatini 6–3, 6–3 for Olympic gold.

items.question: Which achievement did Steffi Graf add to winning all four majors in 1988 to complete the "Golden Slam"?
items.explain: The Golden Slam means winning all four majors and Olympic singles gold in the same year. Graf was the first to do it, in 1988.

items.question: Whom did Steffi Graf beat 6–0, 6–0 in the 1988 French Open final?
items.explain: Graf beat Natasha Zvereva 6–0, 6–0 in the final at Roland Garros in 1988.
